note: Demo rides served at /v1/rides (ADR-043). A short list of roads worth knowing, each one a real stretch of road rather than a town, so picking one plans the ride that made the road famous. The app plans these in one tap -- this is what a new rider sees before they have given us a location. Every entry is verified against the live graph by `tools/check_rides.py`, which asserts the plan actually contains the road the entry names: an entry whose coordinates are slightly off still plans, it just quietly rides somewhere else. `country` exists from the first entry because the graph is US-only today and will not always be -- an entry added before its graph exists cannot plan at all.

rides.name: Tail of the Dragon
rides.blurb: 318 curves in 11 miles. The road that put a name to the whole idea.

rides.name: Million Dollar Highway
rides.blurb: Over Red Mountain Pass at 11,000 ft, with no guardrail and nothing but air beside you.

rides.name: Beartooth Highway
rides.road: US 212, Red Lodge to Cooke City
rides.blurb: Switchbacks to 10,947 ft at Beartooth Pass. Shut by snow for half the year.

rides.name: Cherohala Skyway
rides.blurb: The Dragon's quieter neighbour: longer, higher, and you can see where you're going.

rides.name: Angeles Crest Highway
rides.blurb: Sixty miles of mountain road that starts in the suburbs of Los Angeles.

rides.name: Palomar South Grade
rides.road: S6, Lake Henshaw to Palomar Mountain
rides.blurb: Hairpin after hairpin up the mountain, and a telescope at the top.

rides.name: Palos Verdes Switchbacks
rides.blurb: Short, tight and well laid out, with the Pacific underneath you.

rides.name: Seven Lakes Drive
rides.road: Seven Lakes Drive, Harriman State Park
rides.blurb: An hour out of Manhattan and suddenly there are corners.
